title: CORS Wildcard and Error Information Disclosure in Edge Function
description: The scrape-fragrantica edge function sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (wildcard CORS), allowing any website to invoke it. Additionally, error messages from `error.message` are returned directly to the client, potentially leaking internal implementation details (Deno runtime errors, stack traces, file paths).
impact: Any website can call the edge function, using it as a free proxy. Error messages may reveal internal paths, runtime versions, or dependency information useful for further attacks.
mitigation: Restrict CORS to specific allowed origins. Sanitize error messages before returning to client — log full errors server-side, return generic messages to client.
critic_reasoning: The edge function is deployed with wildcard CORS. Any website can invoke it. This is a live configuration issue, though the practical impact is lower than the other findings.
outrage_commentary: Wildcard CORS is a common misconfiguration. The error disclosure is a secondary concern. Practical exploitation requires a motivated attacker to host a malicious page.
executive_summary: The edge function uses wildcard CORS, allowing any website to invoke it as a proxy. Error messages may leak internal implementation details.
